title: The Filthy Magic of Studio 54
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the history of Studio 54, the New York City disco nightclub at 254 West 54th Street. They trace the building's history as an opera house and CBS studio, the founders Steve Rubell and Ian Schrager and their earlier disco Enchanted Garden in Queens, the club's 1977 opening night and door policy, celebrity crowd and wild parties, the 1978 IRS raid and tax evasion convictions, and the club's closing in February 1980. They close with the hotel business that followed, Rubell's death, Schrager's 2017 pardon, and a listener email about widowed sheriffs.
topics: Halston birthday party Bianca Jagger horse

segments.title: Opening banter and cultural legacy
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode, joke about Studio 54 documentaries and movies, and discuss why the club remains iconic: it closed at its peak, and it was both a haven for gay and trans patrons and a symbol of vapid excess.

segments.title: Building history and founders' background
segments.summary: The building at 254 West 54th Street was an opera house, then a CBS studio (Studio 52) that moved to Los Angeles and sat empty in 1977. Steve Rubell and Ian Schrager, Brooklyn friends from Syracuse, took it over. Rubell overextended himself with steakhouses, and the two co-owned discos in Queens and Boston.

segments.title: Enchanted Garden and silent partner Jack Dushey
segments.summary: Rubell and Schrager gave up their Boston share to get full ownership of Enchanted Garden in Queens, a template for Studio 54 with themed parties. They met Jack Dushey, who became a silent partner and provided about half a million dollars. The street was seedy, and they formed Broadway Catering Corporation and converted the theater in six weeks.

segments.title: Design, sound, and publicity
segments.summary: The club reused the old theater's stage, proscenium, and lighting rig. Richard Long, a sound system veteran, was hired, and publicist Carmen D'Alessio built buzz. Paid PR people were rewarded for placing photos of celebrities in newspapers. The club had 85-foot ceilings, capacity about 2,000, and an 11,000 square foot dance floor with a mezzanine and balcony.

segments.title: Opening night, April 26, 1977
segments.summary: Opening night on Tuesday, April 26, 1977 drew an hour-long line. Eighteen thousand people applied for membership cards and about three thousand got them before opening. Cover was around ten dollars. A doctor handing out Quaaludes sparked a sidewalk party.

segments.title: Quaaludes, celebrities, and Halston's party
segments.summary: Hosts describe the effects of Quaaludes and note that patrons were mostly on uppers. Brooke Shields attended with Robin Leach. The Monday after opening, Halston threw Bianca Jagger's thirtieth birthday party, featuring a white horse, which Bianca Jagger later disputed riding around the club. Hosts note the party put the club on the map.

segments.title: Liquor permits, party costs, and the owners' roles
segments.summary: The club operated on daily one-day catering liquor permits for a year, and once permits were denied and only juice and soda were served. Private parties cost tens of thousands to around $100,000. Rubell was the public host and Schrager the behind-the-scenes figure, and they skimmed cash.

segments.title: Door policy and celebrity exclusion
segments.summary: Rubell selected guests at the door like casting a play, aiming for a mix of people. Head doorman Mark Berninger, nineteen, was the highest-paid staff member, which discouraged bribes. Henry Winkler and others were turned away, and Chic wrote the song Le Freak after being refused entry.

segments.title: Guest lists and door stories
segments.summary: The door list included categories such as no-goods, paying guests, comps, and NFUs. Rubell disliked polyester and told people to wear cotton. Stories included people climbing from other buildings with subway maps and a man found dead after trying to crawl through an air vent.

segments.title: Hours and famous regulars
segments.summary: The club was open Tuesday through Sunday from 10 pm until about 6 am. Regulars included Liza Minnelli, Halston, Bianca Jagger, Andy Warhol, and Truman Capote. Divine, Grace Jones, and Disco Sally, a 77-year-old dancer, were also noted.

segments.title: Animal parties and themed Halloween nights
segments.summary: The club hosted a Dolly Parton country western party with live animals, a Liz Taylor birthday party, and a Valentino party. Halloween was a big night where good costumes improved entry chances, including a Hieronymus Bosch theme.

segments.title: 1978 IRS raid, tax evasion, and prison
segments.summary: Rubell boasted about profits. An informant said the owners skimmed about 80 percent of the money. In December 1978, about thirty IRS agents raided the club, and Schrager arrived with cooked and uncooked books and cocaine. Attorney Roy Cohn advised staging a mess. Dushey testified against them. Rubell and Schrager pleaded guilty in November 1979 and each served about a year.

segments.title: Studio 54 closing and hotel business
segments.summary: Studio 54 closed February 4, 1980 with a farewell party. After prison, Rubell and Schrager bought into hotels and launched boutique hotels starting in 1984 with Morgan's, after buying the space from Mark Fleischmann. Hosts discuss the boutique hotel formula.

segments.title: Palladium, Rubell's death, and Schrager's pardon
segments.summary: The owners opened the Palladium nightclub, partly to fund hotels. Steve Rubell died of AIDS complications in 1989. Ian Schrager received a presidential pardon in 2017 from Barack Obama for his felony conviction.

segments.title: Listener mail: widowed sheriffs
segments.summary: A listener from Kentucky, Sean Herron, wrote an addendum about widows being appointed sheriff after their husbands die, citing Mary Roach and Florence Thompson, who oversaw the last public hanging. Hosts thank him.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and remind listeners how to send cool emails. The show is a production of iHeartRadio.
